authorizationReference: Owner instruction of 2026-09-17 authorising the Grade-A production rollout to expungement.ai, naming reviewed migrations among the covered operations, and authorising this record to be written from the readback's actual run, findings and migration hashes after it succeeded. Measured impact is not automatically approved impact; the measured impact here is nothing at all, so there is no loss or invalidation to escalate.

incidentEvidence.finding: Production already carries positions 17 through 26 of this chain. Exactly one forward migration is absent: 20260917090000_consumer_promotion_codes.sql, which replaces the consumer_briefcase_items paid-row constraint that hardcoded amount_cents = 5000 with a reconciliation rule over regular_price_cents and discount_cents, and adds those two columns. Until it is applied, a discounted order cannot be recorded as paid in Production at all, because a 40%-off or 100%-off order collects something other than 5000 cents and the old constraint refuses the row.

preApplyChecks.frozenHashes: All 11 files at application c88f10341fec848b3f6f4dec9fc3381e6eea0530 hash to the values the control pins. The Stripe catalog-product correction changed no file under supabase/, so every migration hash this record pins is byte-identical to the 0fee79bd127eb3dc072c2a35945177fa7e7b6683 release that applied them; re-pinning the application SHA restates which application the record belongs to, not which migrations it authorises.
preApplyChecks.ledgerReconciliation: The ledger holds 23 versions and the recovered 13-version baseline is present with no unknown rows. Positions 17 through 26 are present in order, the prefix is ordered and there are no unsafe gaps, so the single missing file cannot clobber a later definition. Outside this chain, 20260822180000 has neither a ledger row nor its object and is never replayed here; the three 2026-08-25 Clinic files have no ledger rows and their objects are present.
preApplyChecks.prerequisites: packet_render_jobs, consumer_pending_screening_results, consumer_briefcase_items, screening_sessions, clinic_events, enqueue_packet_render_job and consumer_packet_payment_authority are all present.
preApplyChecks.backups: Supabase Management API, run 35207467289: PITR disabled; WAL-G enabled (us-east-1); no completed backup listed and no physical backup window, so no API-confirmed restore point exists. The one migration this apply adds only adds two columns and replaces a CHECK constraint; it deletes nothing and rewrites no row values.
preApplyChecks.existingRowEffect: Read as counts without writing. 51 stored pending results, 34 claimed under the old scheme. Zero would gain a Briefcase matter link, zero would become CLAIMED and zero would become REVOKED -- broken out, zero claimed without a provable matter, zero unexpired unclaimed, zero expired unclaimed, zero created in the last 24 hours. Two live pending rows and no expired ones are kept untouched. The row-affecting migration in this chain is 20260828100000, and Production applied it in the previous release, which is why nothing is left for it to do.

rollbackApplication.why: 20260917090000 replaces the legacy 14- and 15-argument record_consumer_packet_payment signatures with unconditional invalid_payment_evidence refusals, so that a caller which cannot state the regular price and the discount cannot record a discounted order at full price. The rollback application calls those legacy signatures, so after this migration it settles nothing. The deployment remains a valid AVAILABILITY rollback -- the site serves, screening and claiming work -- and is not a valid payment rollback. Recovery from a failed activation is forward, onto an application that calls the reconciling signature; an order stranded meanwhile is settled by replaying its Stripe event through the idempotent reconciliation path, never by reversing this migration or restoring the retired writer.
rollbackApplication.exposureWindow: Opens when the migration is applied and closes when activation promotes the new application. During it, Production serves the rollback application and Stripe keeps completing orders the application cannot settle.

acceptedRevocation.basis: Measured, not carried forward. Run 35207467289 read every bucket back from Production without writing and found all three empty, so the accepted maximum for each is the measured zero rather than a ceiling with room in it. The migrate phase re-reads the same counts and refuses before any write if a bucket exceeds its maximum, which here means it refuses to revoke even one row. The previous release's ceiling of 15 expired unclaimed rows is deliberately not carried over: those rows were revoked then, and this chain's only missing file revokes nothing.

The remedy was a ledger-only signature for 19, the superseded_artifacts column for 26, a static uniqueness check and a late-apply clobber guard, plus one executeDespiteLedgerRow re-execution of 20260901115000.

executeDespiteLedgerRowThen.whyNotCarriedForward: That re-execution was for a ledger row recorded without an execution in the previous release.
